result.title: Stability and Diversity of Networked Self-Consuming Generative Ecosystems
result.comment: Published as a conference paper at NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: The widespread deployment of generative AI has made it increasingly difficult to distinguish synthetic content from real data. Consequently, synthetic data is inevitably incorporated into the training pipelines of future model generations, forming a self-consuming training loop. Prior work has studied the effects of such recursive self-consuming training, but analyses have largely been limited to isolated models, where a model consumes only its own synthetic data, or to simplified interactions between two models. This paper takes a first step toward understanding networked self-consuming generative models, in which multiple models consume synthetic data generated by one another through complex interaction pathways. We introduce a theoretical framework representing models as nodes in a directed, weighted graph, with edge weights governing the flow of synthetic data among models. Using this framework, we analyze the long-term behavior of networked models under retraining dynamics, establishing conditions for convergence and characterizing the resulting fixed points. We further investigate how the system's long-term stability and diversity are shaped by each model's access to real data, cross-model data consumption, and the structure of the interaction graph.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文将多个自我消耗的生成模型建模为有向加权图上的节点，分析递归重训练下合成数据跨模型流动时的收敛条件、不动点以及长期稳定性与多样性如何受真实数据可得性和图结构影响。
